claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: basically tries to forecast what we call macro trends we try and forecast economic cycles and how our set classes will will behave through those
claims.claim: Caxton's macro approach forecasts economic cycles and asset-class behaviour, buying what it expects to rise and selling what it expects to fall.
claims.direction: long assets expected to rise, short those expected to fall
claims.testable: partly - discretionary forecasts, hard to replicate

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: our investment horizon is several weeks to several months and that can extend out um to be a year
claims.claim: Typical holding horizon is several weeks to several months, sometimes up to a year.
claims.testable: yes - horizon is a stated parameter

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: greed to participate in trends and fear of losing uh two big psychological factors that affect day-to-day life
claims.claim: Trends persist and then reverse because participants fear missing out and fear losing too much, so psychology matters as much as economics.

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: all of those people have been able to combine a really great fundamental
claims.claim: The best macro traders combine fundamental understanding of economies, understanding of how policymakers decide, and a read on what other traders are doing.

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: increasingly computers and algorithms and coding have taken an increasing share
claims.claim: Hedge fund money is increasingly run by algorithms (human decisions reduce to rules), but the best people combine coded or scraped inputs with human intuition.

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: we had some web scraping set up monitoring a number of cases that were getting reported around
claims.claim: Caxton scraped daily case counts worldwide in real time; a spike in Italy on a Saturday morning in late February 2020 showed the virus had spread beyond China, a month before UK lockdown.
claims.indicator: web-scraped Covid case counts by country
claims.testable: yes - scraped case counts are a testable signal

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: the us equity market lost 35 of its value in six weeks
claims.claim: Covid caused a 35% US equity fall in six weeks, after which central banks cut rates to zero and restarted QE.

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: many of the lessons that i learned watching my colleagues back in 1987 were very helpful and useful in 2008
claims.claim: Past crashes (1987, 2008) and historical pandemics (Spanish flu, plague) give templates for how crises unfold and spread, useful for later ones.

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: it's going to become a really central part of all investing
claims.claim: ESG will become central to investing, unlike niche exclusion-based socially responsible investing, because voters care about climate and its damage is seen as proven.
claims.testable: partly - ESG flows and performance data exist

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: people are only going to want to invest their savings and their pensions in companies and in industries that make the world a better place
claims.claim: A large asset manager sees ESG as a commercial opportunity: savers and consumers will favour sustainable companies, and weak governance tends to coincide with poor social and environmental practice.

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: i probably get half of the things wrong that i forecast my skill set is not to let it bother me to sell the things that aren't working to keep the things which are working
claims.claim: A macro forecaster is right only about half the time; profits come from cutting losers quickly, keeping winners and making sure losses on losers are smaller than gains on winners.
claims.testable: yes - win rate and payoff ratio testable

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: most of the people in my company close down nearly all their positions their investment positions before they go on holiday for a week or two weeks
claims.claim: Caxton staff typically close nearly all positions before holidays to avoid unmonitored risk, although Law himself keeps positions and follows markets (markets trade from Sunday 6pm to Friday late evening).

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: artificial intelligence and quantitative techniques and algorithms have taken the place of human functions
claims.claim: Machine learning does repetitive pattern-reaction work, but the big opportunities arise in new situations (such as politics) that models cannot learn from past data.

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: the u.s stock market fell by six seven eight percent during asian hours
claims.claim: After the 2016 US election result, US equity futures fell 6-8% in Asian hours on the consensus view that Trump would hurt growth, then reversed within 12 hours as markets realised the assumption was wrong.
claims.indicator: US equity futures overnight on election night 2016
claims.conditions: event shock where consensus assumption is wrong

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: the quantitative machines the artificial intelligence the machine
claims.claim: Quant and machine-learning strategies lost heavily following election-night poll outcomes, while a few discretionary traders who bet on Trump tax cuts made a lot of money.

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: although crises take a time to develop the markets literally flip a switch one day from ignoring events to panicking about them
claims.claim: Markets ignore developing crises until they abruptly flip to panic (Covid data existed in late December, Hubei locked down mid-January, markets reacted only after the Italy ski weekend), so risk must be watched before the price reacts.
claims.indicator: early crisis data vs market reaction
claims.testable: yes - lag between news and price reaction can be tested

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: history suggests that crises always happen um they happen when nobody really expects them
claims.claim: Crises always occur and arrive when unexpected, so businesses and investors should build resilience, and post-2008/Covid investors are more skittish.

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: pension funds you know look for alternative sources of investment you know they can only hold so many equities and so many bonds and hedge funds offer them a diversified means of investing
claims.claim: Hedge fund assets are now almost entirely pension money: pensions can only hold so much in equities and bonds, so they allocate to hedge funds as a diversifier, a structural demand source for macro and other uncorrelated strategies.
claims.direction: steady pension inflows to hedge funds
claims.conditions: pension funds need diversification beyond stocks and bonds

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: size of the hedge fund industry is 3 trillion globally which sounds like a lot and it is but you know the global assets under management across all equity markets and bonds is more of the order of 100 trillion
claims.claim: The hedge fund industry is about $3 trillion against roughly $100 trillion in global equity and bond assets, i.e. about 3% of the investable universe, so its market footprint is small relative to the whole.
claims.indicator: hedge fund AUM vs global AUM

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: when the equity market lost 25 of its value over a couple of days
claims.claim: The October 1987 crash (about 25% in a couple of days, as he recalls) came in his first month in the City; the experience of that crash gave lessons that were reused in 2008 and 2020.

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: the massive government stimulus the furloughing of workers paying people's bills mortgage holidays business loans and so forth all designed to avert what would have been a repeat of history from the 1930s
claims.claim: Alongside central bank easing, governments launched massive fiscal support (furloughs, bill payment, mortgage holidays, business loans) explicitly to avoid a repeat of the 1930s depression, so the policy response to a shock is now fiscal as well as monetary.

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: employees are going to reclaim two or three hours of every day to do interesting stuff in rather than commuting employers again to save because they're not going to have to um rent or buy such large office buildings
claims.claim: Covid fast-forwarded working from home by perhaps 10-20 years: employees save commuting time and employers need less office space, a structural shift away from large office buildings.

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: then we had the great financial crisis in 2008 the after effects of which are still being felt i think in in society partly as a consequence of austerity that the government pursued
claims.claim: The post-2008 austerity prolonged the societal after-effects of the financial crisis, in contrast with the 2020 response, which was fiscal expansion.

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: if you borrowed too much money to run your business you were probably going to go bankrupt if the if the government hadn't hadn't helped
claims.claim: Covid showed that overleveraged businesses face bankruptcy in a sudden shock unless the government steps in; business can cease overnight, so leverage must be sized for events nobody forecasts.
claims.testable: yes - default rates vs leverage in 2020

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: it's set up on the do not disturb function so only certain people can call me at any time and if something happens somewhere my phone rings
claims.claim: He manages 24/7 market risk with an escalation filter: the phone is on do-not-disturb with only named callers allowed through, so it rings only about ten times a year when something material happens.
claims.conditions: markets open Sunday evening to Friday night

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: i couldn't live with myself have i missed a major investment theme coming to fruition that i've been working on for six months
claims.claim: He does not flatten positions for holidays because missing the payoff of a theme developed over six months costs more than the stress of staying in; flattening trades risk reduction against missing slow-developing theme payoffs.

claims.speaker: Andrew Law
claims.quote: the stock market through to cavite 19 earlier this year one of us strongest and best performances ever over that three year period since donald trump became president
claims.claim: After the wrong first-night consensus that Trump would hurt growth, US equities had one of their strongest three-year runs until Covid, showing that consensus reaction to a political shock can be badly wrong and that the opportunity lies in forecasting policy (tax cuts) rather than reacting to headlines.
claims.testable: yes - event study of election-night moves
